rows.label: New money raised as % total money moved
rows.explainer:
From AIM's Effective Giving Incubation Report: 'Further, we find good evidence that the percentage of money raised that is
counterfactual (i.e. would not have otherwise been donated) is about 50% of the total
raised'.

Maybe charity evaluators raise less new funding than effective giving organizations. If they are 50%, maybe 35% is a reasonable assumption. https://9475dbf4-555e-4808-9886-5f8ee815cc82.usrfiles.com/ugd/9475db_d06fa170d29349318fe61cd87f1d5faa.pdf

rows.label: Presumed cost-effectiveness ratio of identified opportunties
rows.explainer: Multiplier Considering the update to GiveWell's analysis of cost-effectiveness for GiveDirectly we subjectively assume that the evaluator will comfortably find opportunities for funding in the 3x bar - we think this is a conservative assumption. For example, Founders Pledge estimated that Imagine Worldwide - a Malawian education charity - is 10.9 times as cost-effective as GiveDirectly, and believes TaRL Africa 'is slightly more cost-effective due to its lower cost' (Albinsky, 2023). The figure here is calculated as 10x GiveWell's pre-November 2024 estimate for GiveDirectly (which significantly increased their expectations of its cost-effectiveness).

Share of the full cost paid in cash

rows.label: Units of value per dollar
rows.explainer: Ambitious Impact counts income in years of doubled consumption. A doubling for a year is ln 2 of log-consumption, which is one GiveWell unit of value at the shared value of income, so the result ranks with the GiveWell models. With credit by share of resources, times the share of the full cost paid in cash (staff's forgone pay is the rest).

native.unit: years of doubled consumption per $1,000 (expected, with 56% chance of success)

summary: Ambitious Impact's 2025 estimate for a new evaluator that finds and recommends highly cost-effective livelihoods charities, moving donors' money to them. The idea Better Futures Guide was founded to run. Its bottom line is the years of doubled consumption per $1,000 of the evaluator's costs, from new and shifted donations, weighted by its chance of success.
